transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! I'm feeling okay, but I do have a few questions about my recovery. First, I was wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing light gardening, such as watering or gentle weeding, about 1 week after your surgery. However, it's best to avoid bending, lifting, or strenuous activities for a month. Also, be sure to wear protective eyewear when gardening to avoid getting any debris in your eyes.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you. Another question I have is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using your preservative-free eye drops four times daily to help with dryness and discomfort. It's usually recommended to start using them right after surgery, so you've likely already been given some. If you're running low, you can ask your GP for a refill.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Yes, it's normal to have some sensitivity to bright light after cataract surgery, especially in the first few weeks. Wearing sunglasses when you're going outside can help reduce the discomfort. However, if the sensitivity is severe or you're experiencing significant pain, we may need to assess it further.
transcript.delivered: Yes, it's normal to have some sensitivity to bright light after cataract surgery, especially in the first few weeks.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information, Dora. I don't have any more questions right now, but I appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions. Before we go, I just want to confirm that all your questions have been answered. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct. Thanks again for your assistance!
